pack.title: Religion Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Provide reviewer knowledge for GCAM religion, sanctities, holy places, holy books, prophets, companions, scholars, rituals, symbols, unity, and sectarian harm using the existing article structure.
required_evidence: religious insult / mockery | minimum: A literal insult, slur, or degrading phrase targeting the religion, its sanctities, prophets, or sacred texts. | strong: A direct attack, repeated mockery, or hostile framing that unmistakably targets the protected religious concept. | weak: A coded slight, indirect jab, or short hostile phrase that still clearly points to the protected concept. | insufficient: A neutral mention, condemnation, historical discussion, or academic explanation with no attack or endorsement.

desecration / disrespect | minimum: A literal act, line, or description showing desecration of a holy place, holy book, or sacred symbol. | strong: A direct statement that treats the sacred object or place as worthless, dirty, or expendable. | weak: A brief harmful reference that implies desecration but leaves the details to context. | insufficient: A neutral description of the place or object, or a warning about desecration rather than endorsement.

incitement / sectarian division | minimum: A literal call to divide believers, attack religious communities, or spread sectarian hostility. | strong: Language that normalises exclusion, hatred, or communal fracture as desirable or necessary. | weak: A short hostile phrase that still clearly seeks division even if the wording is coded. | insufficient: Debate, criticism, historical analysis, or description of existing disagreement without urging hostility.

misrepresentation / distortion | minimum: A literal false claim about prophets, scholars, rituals, holy books, or religious beliefs used as a harmful assertion. | strong: A repeated or emphatic distortion that is presented as if it were true. | weak: A short misleading statement that clearly bends the religious meaning. | insufficient: A scholarly correction, a question, or a documentary reference that does not adopt the false claim.

glorification / hate speech | minimum: A literal praise of abusive conduct toward religion or its adherents. | strong: A slogan, chant, or support statement that clearly celebrates harm. | weak: A coded or abbreviated endorsement that still clearly points toward hostility. | insufficient: A quote, condemnation, or warning that does not endorse the abuse.
insufficient_evidence: A neutral historical reference to a religious event.
A documentary or academic explanation that does not endorse the harmful meaning.
A quoted line that is clearly framed as evidence or criticism rather than endorsement.
A classroom or lecture context that explains the concept without attacking it.
reviewer_heuristics: Anchor the finding to the exact literal phrase that carries the religious meaning.
Treat direct insult, mockery, and desecration as the strongest signals.
Separate condemnation or scholarship from endorsement.
Use narrative framing to distinguish quotation, documentary, court, and historical mention from actual attack.
Prefer the most specific article: article 1 for sanctities and holy places, article 2 for prophets and companions, article 3 for religion and unity.
If the text is academic, historical, or documentary, do not force a violation unless the line clearly attacks religion.
Treat sectarian division as a religion-domain concern when the line turns communities against one another.
positive_examples: Direct insult: إساءة صريحة إلى النبي أو القرآن داخل الحوار.
Direct desecration: تمزيق المصحف أمام الناس مع تمجيد الفعل.
Sectarian incitement: تحريض صريح على تقسيم المؤمنين وإثارة العداوة بينهم.
Mockery of sanctities: السخرية من المقدسات الدينية بوصفها بلا قيمة.
Prophet defamation: اتهام الرسول بالكذب كحقيقة مباشرة داخل النص.
Holy place abuse: وصف المسجد بالدنس مع دعوة إلى إهانته.
Symbol humiliation: إهانة الرموز الدينية لتشجيع الازدراء.
Religious hate speech: خطاب يضعف احترام الدين ويشجع على الكراهية.
negative_examples: Neutral historical mention: يتحدث الوثائقي عن واقعة قديمة دون دعم أو سخرية.
Educational lecture: المعلم يشرح معنى المقدسات الدينية لتجنب الإساءة إليها.
Academic comparison: يناقش الباحث أوجه الاختلاف بين المدارس الفقهية.
Court testimony: يكرر الشاهد عبارة الإهانة داخل جلسة قانونية بوصفها دليلًا.
Quoted speech: يقتبس الراوي إساءة شخصية أخرى دون تبنيها.
Condemnation: الشخصية تدين الإساءة الدينية وتصفها بأنها خطأ.
News report: يذكر الخبر الحادثة بوصفها خبرًا لا دعوة.
Fictional rejection: يطرح الشرير عبارة مسيئة ثم ترفضها القصة بوضوح.
common_false_positives: A documentary or news report about a religious controversy that is purely informational.
A court transcript that repeats harmful wording as evidence.
A teacher or scholar explaining why a phrase is wrong.
A fictional villain line that the story later condemns.
A historical reference to an old sectarian conflict.
A respectful debate between scholars about doctrine.
A phrase about order or discipline that is not aimed at religion itself.

glossary_relationships.note: Strong anchor for the core religion concept.
Relevant when sacred matters are insulted or defended.
Strong when the text targets prophets or messengers.
Relevant for Quran or other sacred text references.
Relevant for mosques and sacred spaces.
Relevant when the text targets revered companions.
Relevant when the text attacks or praises religious authorities.
Relevant when rites or worship practices are discussed.
Relevant for hijab, emblems, icons, or sacred markers.
Relevant when the text encourages cohesion or respect.
Relevant when the text encourages sectarian conflict.
Relevant for hostile or degrading religious speech.

article_mapping.note: Use for holy places, holy books, symbols, or sanctity abuse.
Use for insult, defamation, or disrespect toward prophets and companions.
Use for attacks on the religion itself, sectarian harm, or public religious hostility.

reporting_guidance: Report the shortest exact phrase that carries the insult, desecration, misrepresentation, or incitement.
Prefer the most specific article and keep article 3 secondary when article 1 or 2 is stronger.
Explain why the text is religion-relevant in narrative terms: what is being attacked, defended, quoted, or described.
If the context is documentary, educational, courtroom, news, or explicit condemnation, say so clearly and do not overstate the finding.
Use a review-only outcome when the text is religion-related but still ambiguous after context analysis.
